newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Gov pledges to spend $250 mln on education.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Gov pledges to spend $250 mln on education.

text.p: New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman pledged Tuesday to spend up to $250 million to achieve the level of aid the state Supreme Court ordered earlier this month for 28 poor school districts.
Whitman also ordered rigorous accountability for the extra spending, including state-appointed auditors.

"Every New Jersey taxpayer deserves to know that we are spending their dollars wisely," she said. "I continue to believe that fiscal parity is not the way to provide every New Jersey child with a thorough and efficient education."
The Supreme Court ruled on May 14, however, that the reforms Whitman proposed as a substitute for cash -- setting core curriculum standards -- did not lessen the need for equal spending power.

In 1990, the high court identified 28 districts it said had special needs, and in 1994 it ordered the state to equalize their per pupil spending with the average of the state's most affluent districts by September 1997. Its latest order held Whitman to that deadline, ruling that her reforms were helpful but not sufficient.

Whitman said no taxes needed to be raised to meet the $250 million target. Revenues on existing taxes are running at least $215 million ahead of budget projections, and the governor said her proposed $2.8 billion pension bond sale will make the problem "manageable" at $100 million.
That plan, however, has met stiff resistance in the state Legislature.

The governor's original pension bond plan was to borrow $3.4 billion that would have enabled her to forgo $647 million in contributions to the state's four pension funds. That idea has since been pared to $2.75 billion with a $590 million budget benefit.
But many lawmakers have said the changes are still probably not enough to win passage.
Whitman on Tuesday repeated her call for passage of the bond deal, saying the money is needed to meet the state's new spending needs.
